title: Nx failed run output tail
description: Schema-first contract of the output tail of one Nx invocation. Nx does not hand a failed task's output back to its caller, it streams it to the standard output and error of the `nx` process, so the repo adapter keeps the last `maximumTailCharacters` characters of everything that process printed (in arrival order, stdout and stderr together) plus every line that names a refusal class by its own words, kept when it arrives (a failed task may print its refusal long before the invocation ends, while its independent siblings keep printing progress for megabytes, so the tail alone forgets the evidence), and, when the invocation failed, classifies that tail like the Bazel lane classifies the tail of a failed action: a task that yielded because its implementation is outdated ends the invocation with the stale implementation error (the outermost command starts again), a nested command that announced its own restart (it exits 75, which Nx reports as an ordinary task failure) counts as such a task, a task whose inputs were edited while it ran makes the lane run the invocation again (the `build` layer of the churn policy; Nx's own cache makes the rerun execute only the tasks that did not finish).

Policy.description: Authored numbers. `maximumTailCharacters`: the bounded tail kept per invocation. `maximumEvidenceLines` and `maximumEvidenceLineCharacters`: the bounded set of lines kept besides the tail, each decided when it arrives.

Summary.description: Authored numbers and texts of the summary that an Nx run leaves when it ends in failure. `reasonPattern`: the first line of a failed task's output that matches it is its reason, otherwise its last line. `maximumTasks`: tasks named in full. The verdict says whether another rerun of the whole run is likely to help: `inputs` (the task read files a peer was editing), `implementation` (the build implementation is outdated, so the command starts again with the current one), `no` (the task itself failed).

en.header: Nx run failed: {failed} task(s) did not succeed after {reruns} rerun(s) of the whole run.
en.notRun: Not run because a task they depend on failed ({count}): {tasks}
en.inputs: another rerun is likely to help: a peer edited files the task reads
en.implementation: another rerun is likely to help: the command starts again with the current build implementation
en.no: another rerun is unlikely to help: the task itself failed

de.header: Nx-Lauf fehlgeschlagen: {failed} Aufgabe(n) gelang(en) nach {reruns} Wiederholung(en) des ganzen Laufs nicht.
de.notRun: Nicht ausgeführt, weil eine Aufgabe, von der sie abhängen, fehlschlug ({count}): {tasks}
de.inputs: eine weitere Wiederholung hilft wahrscheinlich: ein anderer Prozess bearbeitete Dateien, die die Aufgabe liest
de.implementation: eine weitere Wiederholung hilft wahrscheinlich: der Befehl startet mit der aktuellen Build-Implementierung neu
de.no: eine weitere Wiederholung hilft wahrscheinlich nicht: die Aufgabe selbst ist fehlgeschlagen
